title: Get GitHub credentials by device flow, not by asking for a PAT
description:
Operator friction found by running the real install (2026-08-20): tk factory setup stops and asks the operator to hand-create a fine-grained PAT in the GitHub UI. That is the heaviest step in the whole install, and it is the ONLY thing blocking a working factory from completing a run.

The design doc frames the ladder as PAT first because "create your own GitHub App is a heavy first-run ask". That is true when EACH USER registers an App. It is false if ticks ships one.

PROPOSAL: ticks ships a public OAuth client id for a ticks GitHub App and tk factory setup runs the DEVICE FLOW — print a code, the operator approves at github.com/login/device and picks which repositories, done. This is exactly how gh authenticates, and it is both EASIER and NARROWER than the status quo:
  fine-grained PAT: manual UI, one repo, long-lived
  gh auth token:    already present but admin:org and every repo — rejected on blast radius
  device flow:      one browser approval, repos chosen at install, short-lived and refreshable, revoked by uninstalling

THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THIS, do not get it wrong: INSTALLATION tokens (per-run, ~1h, repo-scoped — D11s gold standard) require the Apps PRIVATE KEY. A shared App must never ship that key. USER-TO-SERVER tokens via device flow need only the PUBLIC client id and are still bounded by the Apps installations and permissions. So the shipped rung is user-to-server; the private-key rung stays the documented upgrade for an operator who registers their own App.

Compatible with the deployment model: GitHub hosts the flow, so ticks.sh still operates nothing and no secret is distributed — "a deployable, not a deployment" is intact.

Work: register the App and record the client id in the repo; implement the device flow in tk factory setup with the existing verify-before-store discipline (a live API call against the target repo before anything is written); handle token refresh and expiry, including what a run does when its token expires mid-run; keep --github-token as the manual escape hatch; update docs/factory-credentials.md and the design docs credential ladder so the PAT is the fallback rather than the default.

2026-08-20 07:44 - Small related defect found while configuring with an OAuth token: tk factory status reports the stored credential as 'fine-grained PAT @pengelbrecht' regardless of what it actually is — the label is hardcoded to the rung setup expects. With an OAuth token (gho_) stored, status misdescribes it. That matters for an operator auditing which credential their factory holds and how to revoke it: a PAT is revoked in the tokens UI, an OAuth token via gh auth refresh or by revoking the app. Detect and name the credential type; this tick is adding a third type, so the label must stop being a constant.

acceptance_criteria: tk factory setup obtains a working GitHub credential through the device flow with no PAT creation, and stores it after a live check against the target repo; the credential is bounded to the repositories chosen at install; expiry and refresh are handled, with a documented behaviour for expiry mid-run; --github-token still works; the docs present device flow as the default rung and the self-registered App as the upgrade.
closed_reason: Completed: tk factory setup gets its GitHub credential by device flow instead of a hand-made PAT — one browser approval, repositories chosen at approval, short-lived and refreshable. Shipped rung is user-to-server (public client id only); the installation-token rung stays the documented upgrade for an operator with their own App, because a shared App must never carry the private key. A build with an empty client id keeps the manual PAT walk rather than offering a flow that cannot complete. Registration checklist in docs/factory-credentials.md.
